mainTopic: Aggadah on גלות בבל and the future redemption; then the משנה's rules on who is included in a household's קרבן פסח (orphans, wives, dependents, a partners' slave, a half-slave).
overview: The amud opens with the end of a teaching: גלות בבל was a kindness, because cheap dates let the Jews there learn Torah. עולא visits פומבדיתא and complains that with food so cheap the בבלאי should learn more. Then the dates make him sick, and he praises them instead. רבי אלעזר explains that ישעיהו calls the future מקדש the house of the 'God of יעקב' because it will be a בית, as יעקב called it. רבי יוחנן adds that קבוץ גליות is as great as the day of creation. The גמרא then returns to the משנה. רבי זירא shows that the orphan's case is based on 'שה לבית', not ברירה. Two ברייתות explain who is included in the master's פסח automatically and who can protest by slaughtering their own. Next, רב נחמן resolves a contradiction about a slave owned by two partners. Finally, the גמרא explains the half-slave's case through the משנה ראשונה and the משנה אחרונה, and the quote from בית שמאי continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Dates in בבל make Torah study possible
steps.stepSummary: The end of the earlier teaching: the exiles in בבל would eat dates and be able to learn Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: …dates, and they will engage in Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining in the middle of a statement from the previous section. It finishes the idea that the exile to בבל was a kindness, because there was plenty of food there (dates) and so the Jews could learn Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full statement (which started on the previous amud) says that הקב״ה exiled the Jews to בבל because food was cheap and plentiful there. Dates gave them strength and freed up their time, so they could devote themselves to Torah. The story that comes next is a real-life example of this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: They will engage in / toil in Torah study

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the tail end of a teaching that began on the previous amud, so do not look for a speaker here.

phrases.english: dates, and they will engage in Torah.
phrases.notes: Ending of the previous statement: the exile to Babylonia, where dates were plentiful, enabled Torah study.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement that began earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The plentiful dates of בבל allowed the exiles to support themselves easily and learn Torah.

steps.title: עולא is amazed at how cheap dates are
steps.stepSummary: עולא visits פומבדיתא, hears that a whole basket of dates costs only a third of a זוז, and complains that the בבלאי should be learning more Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא visited פומבדיתא. They brought him a basket of dates. He asked: How many baskets like these can you buy for a זוז? They told him: three for a זוז. He said: A whole basketful of 'honey' for a זוז, and the בבלאי are not busy with Torah?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about עולא, a sage from ארץ ישראל who visited בבל. He hears how cheap dates are and criticizes the local people for not learning more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא uses the same reasoning as the line before: if food is this cheap, people barely need to work. So, he says, they should be spending much more time learning Torah. He calls the dates 'honey' because they are so sweet and good.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage from ארץ ישראל who often traveled to בבל
A זוז, a small silver coin

phrases.english: Ulla happened to come to Pumbedita,
they brought him a basket of dates.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: כַּמָּה כִּי הָנֵי בְּזוּזָא?
phrases.english: He said to them: How many like these for a zuz?
They said to him: Three for a zuz.
He said: A basketful of honey for a zuz,
phrases.notes: He calls the sweet dates 'honey'.

phrases.english: and the Babylonians do not engage in Torah?!
phrases.notes: A complaint: with food this cheap they should be learning more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that shows the cheapness of dates in בבל, the same point made in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עולא's first view: food in בבל is so cheap that the בבלאי have no excuse for not learning more Torah.

steps.title: עולא gets sick and changes his mind
steps.stepSummary: That night the dates make עולא ill. He takes back his criticism and praises the בבלאי for learning Torah despite eating 'poison'.
steps.simpleTranslation: At night the dates hurt him. He said: A basketful of deadly poison costs a זוז in בבל, and still the בבלאי are busy with Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a twist. עולא gets a stomach ache from the dates, so he reverses his opinion and praises the people of בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the dates were 'honey', proof that life was easy. Now the same dates are 'deadly poison', proof that life is hard. So the fact that the בבלאי still learn Torah is a credit to them, not something to complain about.
steps.whatToRemember: The same cheap dates go from 'honey' to 'poison'. Once עולא experienced how hard they were on the body, his complaint turned into praise for the בבלאי's Torah learning.

phrases.english: At night they pained him.
He said: A basketful of deadly poison
for a zuz in Babylonia,
and the Babylonians engage in Torah!
phrases.notes: Now said as praise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses עולא's own complaint from step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The בבלאי deserve praise: they learn Torah even though the food they live on is hard on the body.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say only 'the God of יעקב'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר quotes ישעיהו about the nations going up to 'the house of the God of יעקב' and asks why only יעקב is mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: What is the meaning of the פסוק, 'Many peoples will go and say: Come, let us go up to the mountain of ה׳, to the house of the God of יעקב'? Is He only the God of יעקב, and not the God of אברהם and יצחק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its earlier topic, פסוקים of comfort about the future. רבי אלעזר asks a question about a פסוק. His answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually ה׳ is called the God of all three אבות. So it is strange that ישעיהו names only יעקב. רבי אלעזר assumes the choice of words must be teaching something.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said: What is that which is written:
"And many peoples shall go and say:
phrases.notes: ישעיהו ב:ג

phrases.english: Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord,
to the house of the God of Jacob, etc."

phrases.aramaic: אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב, וְלֹא אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק?
phrases.english: The God of Jacob, and not the God of Abraham and Isaac?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עולא story and returns to the topic of פסוקים of comfort.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does ישעיהו describe the future מקדש as belonging to 'the God of יעקב' only?

steps.title: The מקדש will be a 'house', as יעקב called it
steps.stepSummary: The future מקדש will be described the way יעקב named it, a 'house' (בית אל). It will not be called a 'mountain' as אברהם called it, or a 'field' as יצחק called it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: not like אברהם, about whom 'mountain' is written ('on the mountain of ה׳ He will be seen'); and not like יצחק, about whom 'field' is written ('יצחק went out to pray in the field'); but like יעקב, who called it 'house' ('he called the place בית אל').
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers his own question. Each of the אבות prayed at the place of the מקדש and used a different word for it. The פסוק names יעקב because his word, 'house', is how the place will be described in the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mountain or a field is open and temporary. A house is a lasting home. So mentioning יעקב teaches that the future מקדש will be a permanent dwelling place for the שכינה. The point is not that ה׳ belongs to יעקב more than to the other אבות.

keyTerms.meaning: Mountain: אברהם's word for the place
Field: יצחק's word for the place
To speak / pray (here understood as prayer)
House: יעקב's word for the place

steps.whatToRemember: All three אבות prayed at the place of the מקדש, but each called it something different: הר, שדה, בית. The future מקדש will be a 'בית', a permanent home, as יעקב called it.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not mean ה׳ is not the God of אברהם and יצחק. The verse mentions יעקב only to point to his word for the place, 'house'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the future redemption is pictured as a stable, lasting home for the שכינה, the fullest stage of what the אבות began.

phrases.english: Rather: not like Abraham, about whom 'mountain' is written,
as it is stated: "As it is said this day:
phrases.notes: בראשית כב:יד

phrases.english: On the mountain of the Lord He will be seen";
and not like Isaac, about whom 'field' is written,
as it is stated: "And Isaac went out to pray in the field";
phrases.notes: בראשית כד:סג

phrases.english: but like Jacob, who called it 'house',
as it is stated: "And he called the name of that place
phrases.notes: בראשית כח:יט

phrases.english: Beth-El" (House of God).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יעקב is mentioned because the future מקדש will be described as a 'house', the term יעקב used, rather than 'mountain' (אברהם) or 'field' (יצחק).

steps.title: The ingathering of exiles is as great as the day of creation
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the day of קבוץ גליות is as great as the day שמים וארץ were created. He links a פסוק in הושע to the creation story through the word 'day'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The ingathering of the exiles is as great as the day heaven and earth were created. It says: 'And the children of יהודה and the children of ישראל will gather together, and appoint for themselves one leader, and go up from the land, for great is the day of יזרעאל.' And it is written: 'And there was evening and there was morning, one day.'
steps.whatsHappening: This continues the אגדה about the גלות and the future redemption. רבי יוחנן says the day the exiles are gathered back will be as great as the day of creation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in הושע calls the day of gathering a 'great day' (גדול יום). רבי יוחנן links this 'day' to the 'one day' of creation in בראשית. The point is that the final redemption is like a brand-new creation of the world.

keyTerms.meaning: The ingathering of the exiles, when all Jews return to ארץ ישראל
'The day of יזרעאל', the day of redemption in the נבואה of הושע
'One day', the first day of creation

steps.whatToRemember: This closes the אגדה section. Right after this, the גמרא goes back to the הלכה of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The ingathering of exiles is great
like the day on which heaven and earth were created,
as it says: 'And the children of Judah will be gathered'
'and the children of Israel together'
'and they will appoint for themselves one head'
'and go up from the land'
'for great is the day of Jezreel',
phrases.notes: The word 'day' here is the link to the creation פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״וַיְהִי עֶרֶב וַיְהִי בֹקֶר יוֹם אֶחָד״.
phrases.english: and it is written: 'And there was evening and there was morning, one day.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: גָּדוֹל קִבּוּץ גָּלִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the אגדה about the גלות and the future redemption, adding a final praise of the redemption day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The day of קבוץ גליות equals in greatness the day of creation, derived from the shared word 'day'.

steps.title: Does the orphan case prove ברירה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about an orphan whose guardians each slaughtered a פסח for him. It suggests this case proves the principle of ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'An orphan whose guardians slaughtered for him...' (and he eats wherever he wants). You can learn from this that there is ברירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and tries to prove a big principle from it, called ברירה. This sets up the next step, where רבי זירא rejects the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each guardian brought a פסח for the orphan, yet he only decides later which one to eat from. If his later choice counts, it seems his choice 'reveals' that he belonged to that group from the start. That idea of a later choice revealing what was true all along is ברירה.

keyTerms.meaning: An orphan (here, a minor without a father)
Guardians who manage a minor's affairs
'You can learn from it', a formula introducing a proof
Retroactive clarification: a later choice shows what was true from the start

steps.confusionAlert: ברירה does not mean 'choice' in the simple sense. It means a later decision is treated as if it had been decided at the very beginning.

phrases.english: An orphan on whose behalf guardians slaughtered, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. It continues: he eats in whichever place he wishes.

phrases.english: Learn from it: there is retroactive clarification.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה and returns to the משנה's הלכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the orphan who may eat from whichever guardian's פסח he chooses

steps.title: רבי זירא: it is not ברירה, it is 'שה לבית'
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא rejects the proof. The orphan is included because of the פסוק 'שה לבית', which includes a minor in any case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: 'A lamb for the household', in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא pushes back on the proof. He says the orphan's case works for a different reason, so it proves nothing about ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'שה לבית' teaches that a minor is included in a household's פסח just by belonging to it, with no need for his own decision. So the משנה does not depend on ברירה at all. The question of ברירה stays open.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
'A lamb for the household', in any case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: שֶׂה לַבָּיִת מִכׇּל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof for ברירה offered in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference only. The משנה's ruling still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The orphan's case can be explained by 'שה לבית', which includes a minor automatically, so ברירה is not needed.

steps.title: Who can be included without asking
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains 'שה לבית'. A man may include his minor children and Canaanite slaves in his פסח even without their consent. Adult children, Hebrew slaves and his wife need to agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'A lamb for the household' teaches that a person may bring and slaughter for his minor son and daughter and for his Canaanite slave and maidservant, whether they agree or not. But he may not slaughter for his adult son and daughter, his Hebrew slave and maidservant, or his wife, unless they agree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses the same פסוק as רבי זירא. It lays out who is automatically part of the 'household' for the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Minors and Canaanite slaves are fully tied to the head of the house, so they are included even without agreeing. Adults, Hebrew slaves and a wife are independent people, so they are included only if they agree. This supports רבי זירא's point that a minor needs no choice of his own.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The רבנן taught', the opening of a ברייתא
A non-Jewish slave owned by a Jew, treated as part of the household
A Jewish servant who works for a limited time and stays independent

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the basic rule for joining a קרבן פסח. Household dependents are included automatically, while independent adults must agree.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: 'A lamb for the household':
this teaches that a person brings and slaughters
on behalf of his minor son and daughter
and on behalf of his Canaanite slave and maidservant,
whether with their consent or without their consent.
But he does not slaughter
on behalf of his adult son and daughter
or on behalf of his Hebrew slave and maidservant
or on behalf of his wife,
except with their consent.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שֶׂה לַבָּיִת מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאָדָם מֵבִיא וְשׁוֹחֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the פסוק רבי זירא used, showing how it works in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Minor children and Canaanite slaves may be included in the פסח without consent. Adult children, Hebrew slaves and a wife may be included only with consent.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: the master's קרבן overrides their own
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא repeats the same rules in reverse order. It then adds that if minors or Canaanite slaves slaughtered their own פסח and their master also slaughtered for them, they count with the master's, not their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: A person may not slaughter for his adult son and daughter, his Hebrew slave and maidservant, or his wife, unless they agree. But he may slaughter for his minor son and daughter and his Canaanite slave and maidservant, whether they agree or not. And in all cases where they slaughtered for themselves and their master also slaughtered for them, they fulfill their obligation with the master's קרבן and not with their own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that restates the same rules. Its real new point is at the end: what happens when household members brought their own קרבן but the master also brought one for them. (Step 11 gives the ברייתא's final line.)
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half matches the previous ברייתא, just in the opposite order. The new information is that when any of the household members listed brought their own פסח and the master also slaughtered for them, the master's קרבן wins and their own does not count. The next line limits this with one exception.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Another ברייתא taught', introducing a second ברייתא
Their master, meaning the father or owner

steps.confusionAlert: 'Their master' here includes the father of the children, not only the owner of the slaves. 'וכולן' refers to everyone listed in the ברייתא, including the adults and the wife. That is why the next line must make the wife an exception, and why the גמרא then asks what makes the wife different from the other adults.

phrases.english: It was taught in another baraita:
A person may not slaughter

phrases.aramaic: לֹא עַל יְדֵי בְּנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ הַגְּדוֹלִים
phrases.english: neither on behalf of his adult son and daughter
nor on behalf of his Hebrew slave and maidservant
nor on behalf of his wife,
except with their consent.
But he does slaughter
on behalf of his minor son and daughter
and on behalf of his Canaanite slave and maidservant,
whether with their consent or without their consent,
and all of them who slaughtered, and their master also slaughtered for them,
fulfill their obligation with their master's,
and do not fulfill it with their own,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the first ברייתא's rules and adds a new ruling about competing קרבנות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When any of the listed household members slaughtered their own פסח and the master also slaughtered for them, they fulfill their obligation only with the master's קרבן. The next line gives the exception.

steps.title: The wife is the exception because she can protest
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא from Step 10 ends: if the master slaughtered a פסח for his household, everyone counts with his, except the wife. She can protest and keep her own פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for the wife, who is able to protest.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the ברייתא from the previous step. It adds one exception: the wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Minors and Canaanite slaves count with the master's פסח even if they slaughtered their own. A wife is different because she can protest. She can tell her husband she does not want his support, so her earnings are not his. That gives her her own legal standing, and her own פסח counts.

keyTerms.meaning: To protest; to object and refuse

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ברייתא. It is the last line of the second ברייתא quoted in Step 10.

phrases.english: Except for the wife,
who is able to protest.
phrases.notes: She can say she won't take his support and keep her earnings, so she has her own legal standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in Step 10 by adding its final exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife who protests is not automatically counted with her husband's פסח; her own פסח counts.

steps.title: What makes a wife different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא singles out the wife. Adult children and Hebrew slaves also have independent standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a wife?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the ברייתא's wording. It is setting up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9, adult children, Hebrew slaves and the wife were grouped together as people who need to agree. So why does the exception name only the wife? The question is whether the others are left out of the exception.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why is this case treated separately?

phrases.english: What is different about a wife?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the scope of the exception stated in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the exception is limited to a wife or also covers adult children and Hebrew slaves.

steps.title: The wife and everyone like her
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the wife is only an example. The exception covers everyone similar to her, meaning adult children and Hebrew slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A wife, and all who are similar to her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains that the word 'wife' in the ברייתא is an example, not a limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone with independent legal standing, like a wife, can keep their own פסח. That includes adult children and Hebrew slaves. Minors and Canaanite slaves have no independent standing, so the master's פסח still counts for them.

keyTerms.meaning: And everyone who is similar to her

steps.whatToRemember: Two groups: (1) minors and Canaanite slaves are always counted with the master's פסח; (2) the wife, adult children and Hebrew slaves have their own standing and can keep their own.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A wife, and all who are similar to her.
phrases.notes: That is, adult children and Hebrew slaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִשָּׁה וְכׇל דְּדָמֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The exception extends to all who resemble the wife: adult children and Hebrew slaves.

steps.title: The two halves of the ברייתא seem to contradict
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא suggests that a wife who stays silent is included in her husband's פסח. The beginning says she is included only with her consent, which suggests that silence is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: This itself is difficult. You said: 'Except for the wife, who is able to protest.' So the reason is that she protests. If she does not protest, she fulfills her obligation with her husband's פסח. But the first clause teaches: 'and not on behalf of his wife except with their consent.' So in a silent case she does not fulfill her obligation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a contradiction inside the same ברייתא, comparing its ending with its beginning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ending implies she is out only if she actively protests, so silence means she is in. The beginning implies she is in only if she agrees, so silence means she is out. The two clauses give opposite results for the silent case.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult (an internal contradiction)
The reason is that she protests
An unspecified case, where nothing was said

steps.confusionAlert: The whole question is about the silent wife, who neither agreed nor protested. Keep that case in mind.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
You said: 'Except for the wife —
who is able to protest.'
The reason is that she protests;
so if she does not protest —
she fulfills her obligation with her husband's.
But the first clause teaches:
'And not on behalf of his wife
except with their consent,'
so in an unspecified case she does not fulfill her obligation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from what the exception covers to a contradiction between the ברייתא's two clauses.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the ברייתא (first clause vs. final clause).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading each clause precisely gives opposite rulings for a wife who said nothing: included per the ending, excluded per the beginning.

steps.title: 'With their consent' means presumed consent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'with their consent' does not require an explicit yes. Silence counts as consent. Only an explicit 'no' excludes her.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'only with their consent' mean? Not that they said yes. Rather, even an unspecified case is fine. It comes to exclude only where they said no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by reading the first clause differently, so it matches the ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'With their consent' really means 'not against their will.' Silence counts as agreement, so the silent wife is included. That fits the ending: only a wife who protests ('says no') is out. Both clauses now agree.
steps.whatToRemember: Adult household members (wife, adult children, Hebrew slaves) are counted with the master's פסח by default. Silence counts as consent. Only an explicit 'no', a protest, takes them out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a pattern you will see often: the גמרא rereads one clause of a ברייתא so that it fits the other.

phrases.english: What is 'except with their consent'?
Not that they said 'yes';
rather, even in an unspecified case,
to exclude only where they said 'no'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the first clause's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'With their consent' requires an explicit yes, so a silent wife is excluded.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'With their consent' means not against their will. Silence counts as consent, and only an explicit 'no' excludes her.

steps.title: The case where they slaughtered their own looks like silence, yet the wife is excluded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 15. The ברייתא's case of 'כולם ששחטו' seems to involve no spoken protest. Even so, the wife is excluded 'because she can protest,' which suggests silence does not include her.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at the ברייתא: 'All of them who slaughtered their own, and their master also slaughtered for them, fulfill their obligation with the master's.' That is a case with no spoken protest. Yet it teaches: 'except for the wife, because she can protest.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 15, that silence counts as consent and only an explicit 'no' excludes the wife. It points to a case where the wife said nothing, yet she is still excluded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of 'כולם ששחטו,' nobody said anything; it is a סתמא (unspecified) case. Still, the ברייתא excludes the wife because she 'is able to protest.' That makes it sound as though the mere ability to protest excludes her, even without an actual protest, which contradicts Step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them who slaughtered (their own פסח)
Their master (the head of the household)
In an unspecified case, where nothing was said

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse two different cases. Step 15 discussed the master slaughtering for everyone. Here, the household members slaughtered their own פסח first, and then the master also slaughtered for them.

phrases.english: But surely: 'All of them who slaughtered'
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא from Step 10

phrases.english: and their master slaughtered on their behalf
fulfill their obligation with the master's'
which is an unspecified case (no spoken protest),
and it teaches: except for the wife
because she is able to protest!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כּוּלָּם שֶׁשָּׁחֲטוּ וְשָׁחַט רַבָּן עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 15's claim that silence counts as consent and only an explicit 'no' excludes the wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the 'כולם ששחטו' case there is no spoken protest, yet the wife is excluded. So the mere ability to protest seems to exclude her.

steps.title: Slaughtering her own פסח is itself the strongest protest
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the act of slaughtering one's own פסח counts as a protest. In fact, it is the clearest protest possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Since they slaughtered their own, there is no greater protest than this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. The 'כולם ששחטו' case is not really silence, because slaughtering her own פסח is an action that shows she objects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15's rule stands: silence includes her, and only a protest excludes her. A protest does not have to be spoken, though. Bringing her own פסח shows clearly that she wants her own, not her husband's.
steps.whatToRemember: Silence counts as consent to be included in the husband's פסח. A protest excludes her, and a protest can be an action. Slaughtering her own פסח is the strongest protest of all.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Since they slaughtered (their own)
you have no greater protest than this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כֵּיוָן שֶׁשָּׁחֲטוּ אֵין לְךָ מִיחוּי גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: an action counts as a protest
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'כולם ששחטו' looked like a silent case, so excluding the wife seemed to contradict 'silence equals consent'
steps.terutzMaskana: Slaughtering her own פסח is an active protest, the strongest possible. So the case is not silence at all, and Step 15 stands.

steps.title: Quoting the next line of the משנה: a slave owned by two partners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה, about a slave owned jointly by two partners.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A slave of two partners,' etc.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a heading line that sets up the next discussion. The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a slave owned by two partners, who may not eat from either partner's פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה says this slave may not eat from either partner's פסח, unless it was arranged in advance whose he will eat from. The גמרא is about to compare this ruling with a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. (the quote continues in the משנה)

phrases.english: A slave of two partners, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה as a heading

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave owned by two partners may not eat from either partner's פסח unless this was arranged beforehand.

steps.title: The משנה forbids the jointly owned slave from eating, but a ברייתא lets him choose
steps.stepSummary: רב עינא סבא points out a contradiction to רב נחמן. The משנה says the slave may not eat from either partner's פסח, while a ברייתא says he may eat from whichever one he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עינא סבא pointed out a contradiction to רב נחמן: We learned in the משנה, 'A slave of two partners may not eat from either of theirs.' But a ברייתא teaches: 'If he wants, he eats from this one; if he wants, he eats from that one!'
steps.whatsHappening: Two sources seem to clash. The משנה forbids the slave from eating from either partner's פסח, but the ברייתא lets him pick either one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a classic רמי, setting two sources against each other. One says 'no,' the other says 'yes, your choice.' Both cannot be right about the same case, so the next step will look for a difference between the cases.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction (set two sources against each other)

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב עֵינָא סָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Eina the Elder raised a contradiction to Rav Nachman:
We learned: a slave of two partners
may not eat from either of theirs.
But it was taught: if he wants, he eats from this one,
if he wants, he eats from that one!

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב עֵינָא סָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in Step 18 using a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a jointly owned slave may not eat from either partner's פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly lets the same slave eat from whichever partner's פסח he chooses, which directly contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: Strict partners versus easygoing partners
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the two sources speak about different partners. The משנה deals with partners who are strict with each other, and the ברייתא deals with partners who are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Eina the Elder (some say he called him 'black pot,' a fond name for a hard-working scholar), through me and you this teaching will be settled. The משנה is where the partners are strict with each other. The ברייתא is where they are not strict with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן warmly greets רב עינא and resolves the contradiction. He shows that each source is talking about a different kind of partnership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the partners are strict, each one objects to his half of the slave eating from the other's פסח, so the slave cannot eat from either. When the partners do not mind, the slave may freely choose either one. The two sources do not argue; they describe two different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Black pot,' a fond nickname for a scholar who toils in learning
They are strict with each other, they mind

steps.whatToRemember: A slave owned by two partners: if the partners are strict with each other, he eats from neither (the משנה). If they are not strict, he may eat from whichever one he chooses (the ברייתא).
steps.confusionAlert: 'פתיא אוכמא' (black pot) is not an insult. It is a term of affection for a scholar who works very hard at Torah.

phrases.english: He said to him: Eina the Elder,
and some say: 'black pot,'
phrases.notes: A fond nickname for a hard-working scholar

phrases.english: through me and you this teaching will be settled.
The Mishnah: where they are strict with each other,
the Baraita: where they are not strict with each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עֵינָא סָבָא, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: פַּתְיָא אוּכָּמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source speaks about a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seemed to rule differently about the same slave
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה deals with partners who are strict with each other, so the slave eats from neither. The ברייתא deals with partners who do not mind, so the slave may choose either.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on the half-slave and reading it closely
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about a half-slave, half-free man and infers that he may eat from his own פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says one who is half slave and half free may not eat from his master's פסח. So it is only his master's that he may not eat from. But from his own, he may eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and draws a simple inference from its wording. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says he may not eat from his master's פסח. The גמרא reasons that if he could not eat from his own either, the משנה would have said so. So the משנה implies he may eat from his own פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Half slave and half free man, for example a slave owned by two partners where only one partner freed him

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין
phrases.english: One who is half slave and half free man
may not eat from his master's (Paschal lamb), etc.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: It is specifically from his master's that he may not eat,
but from his own, he may eat.
phrases.notes: The inference drawn from the משנה's wording

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁל רַבּוֹ הוּא דְּלֹא יֹאכַל, אֲבָל מִשֶּׁל עַצְמוֹ יֹאכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the case of the slave of two partners (Steps 18-20) to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A half-slave may not eat from his master's פסח. By inference, he may eat from his own.

steps.title: A ברייתא says he eats from neither
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference with a ברייתא that forbids the half-slave from eating from his own פסח too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: he may not eat from his own, and he may not eat from his master's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. A ברייתא says the half-slave may not eat from any פסח at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 21, the משנה implied that the half-slave may eat from his own פסח. The ברייתא says clearly that he may not. These two sources seem to directly disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught (in a ברייתא)? This opens a challenge from a ברייתא

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a baraita:
He may eat neither from his own
nor from his master's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference made in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that the half-slave may eat from his own פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids him from eating even from his own, which contradicts what the משנה implies.

steps.title: Two different stages of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows the משנה ראשונה and our משנה follows the משנה אחרונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. One source follows the first version of the משנה. The other follows the later version of the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction. The two sources reflect two different stages of the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling on a half-slave's status changed over time. The ברייתא (he eats from neither) matches the משנה ראשונה, when the master still had a real hold on him. Our משנה (he eats from his own) matches the משנה אחרונה, when he came to be treated like a free man for his own פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This opens an answer
The first, original version of a teaching
The later, final version of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: The first כאן refers to the ברייתא, which follows the משנה ראשונה. The second כאן refers to our משנה, which follows the משנה אחרונה. Do not mix them up.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
Here, it is according to the first version of the mishna,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא: he eats from neither

phrases.english: there, it is according to the later version of the mishna.
phrases.notes: Our משנה: he eats from his own

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן כְּמִשְׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה, כָּאן כְּמִשְׁנָה אַחֲרוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the two sources to two different historical stages of the law (משנה ראשונה vs. משנה אחרונה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seem to give two opposite rulings for the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each source is correct for its own stage. The ברייתא reflects the original view, and our משנה reflects the revised view.

steps.title: Citing the משנה where the change is recorded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה showing the two stages: בית הלל first said the half-slave splits his days between his master and himself, and then בית שמאי give their view.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: one who is half slave and half free serves his master one day and himself one day. These are the words of בית הלל. בית שמאי say:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by quoting the משנה where the earlier and later versions appear. The quote continues on the next amud with בית שמאי's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the משנה ראשונה: according to בית הלל, the half-slave alternates days, so the master still owns part of him. That is why the ברייתא says he cannot eat even from his own פסח. בית שמאי's opinion, which the משנה אחרונה ends up following, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned (in a משנה). This introduces a supporting משנה
He serves his master one day

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין —
phrases.english: One who is half slave and half free man
serves his master one day
and himself one day;
this is the statement of Beit Hillel.
Beit Shammai say:
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the claim in Step 23 that there was a first version and a later version.
steps.raayaObject: The existence of a משנה ראשונה and a משנה אחרונה about the half-slave
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה recording בית הלל's original ruling (one day for his master, one day for himself) and בית שמאי's opposing view
